policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'it was thou that leddest out' renders a 2ms 'thou wast'; the ketiv הייתה is a plene spelling of the same 2ms form and the English shows nothing that separates the two spellings. The only note is alternative_rendering ('Or, leader') on a different word. Base qere fallback carries the projection.

Qere הַמּוֹצִיא has the article, ketiv מוציא lacks it; ASV 'that leddest out' is a relative participle rendering that either an articular or anarthrous participle yields. No note maps to this unit. Base qere fallback carries the projection.

Ketiv והמבי differs from qere וְהַמֵּבִיא only by the dropped final aleph, an orthographic variant of the same hiphil participle; ASV 'and broughtest in' cannot distinguish spellings. No note maps to this unit. Base qere fallback carries the projection.

ASV main text 'the lame and the blind, that are hated of David's soul' renders the passive participle construct שְׂנֻאֵי (qere). The textual_variant note 'Another reading is, that hate David's soul' records the active ketiv שנאו as the reading not adopted, so the ASV explicitly distinguishes and follows the qere.

Qere כְּשָׁמְעֲךָ (preposition כ) and ketiv בשמעך (preposition ב) both yield temporal 'when thou hearest'; ASV 'when thou hearest the sound of marching' does not distinguish the preposition. No note on the verse. Base qere fallback carries the projection.
